question: How many orders were placed in January 2018?
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01' AND order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-02-01';
notes: Counts all order statuses. Date is the purchase timestamp. Result taken from the monthly order counts in the profile; re-run to confirm.

question: What was total revenue in 2017?
gold_sql: SELECT SUM(p.payment_value) FROM orders o JOIN order_payments p ON o.order_id = p.order_id WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-01-01';
notes: Revenue = payment_value; delivered orders only; purchase date in 2017. The word revenue is left undefined in the question on purpose: the definition comes from the metrics file at L4. Checked: the three years (46586.33 + 6922900.24 + 8452975.2) add up to 15422461.77, the delivered payment total.

question: Which product category generated the highest revenue?
gold_sql: SELECT COALESCE(t.product_category_name_english, pr.product_category_name, 'unknown') AS category, SUM(i.price) AS revenue FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON i.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products pr ON i.product_id = pr.product_id LEFT JOIN product_category_name_translation t ON pr.product_category_name = t.product_category_name WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered' GROUP BY category ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 1;
notes: Revenue = SUM of order_items.price; delivered orders only. Payments are not used because they cannot be split by category and would multiply rows. Products with no category show as unknown; products whose category has no translation show the Portuguese name. Result taken from the earlier inner-join version; re-run the LEFT JOIN version and confirm. Sanity: all category totals must add up to 13221498.11, the delivered total of item prices.

question: How many distinct customers placed an order in the 90 days before 2018-08-01?
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_unique_id) FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-05-03' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-08-01';
notes: A customer is a person (customer_unique_id), because customer_id changes with every order. All order statuses count, because the question says placed an order, same as Q1. Window is 2018-05-03 up to but not including 2018-08-01 (90 days). Checked: 18551 people in 18780 orders; delivered-only would be 18248 people.
